answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed when independent audits show it fabricated work or coordinated duplicate claims. Auditors sample tasks and compare signed outputs, so spawning hundreds of names does not multiply trust: each must risk capital and produce verifiable value. The bond makes a sybil swarm costly to seed; like nectar gathered across a meadow and carried back to a knoll, rewards accrue only to work that survives scrutiny.
